## What I work on

Most of my work sits where field measurement meets statistical modelling: large
longitudinal wearable and sensor datasets, randomised cooling interventions in
homes and dormitories, and systematic reviews that feed directly into national
heat-health policy. I lead the statistical analysis for two national research
programmes — **Project HEATS** and **Cooling Singapore 2.0** — and work
alongside teams of early career researchers across both.

::: {.grid-cards}
::: {.card-item}
#### Indoor heat and sleep
How bedroom temperature and humidity shape sleep continuity in tropical
homes and dormitories — 122 participants, 10,303 person-nights, three field
waves.

[Explore this research →](research.qmd#heats){.no-rule}
:::

::: {.card-item}
#### Heat vulnerability and advisories
Evidence synthesis behind Singapore's Exertional Heat Vulnerability Index, and
a review of how heat-health advisories are designed and whether they work.

[Explore this research →](research.qmd#ehvi){.no-rule}
:::

::: {.card-item}
#### Physiological strain in the heat
Laboratory responses to controlled heat exposure in children, unacclimatised
adults and older adults, translated into population-tailored guidance.

[Explore this research →](research.qmd#cs20){.no-rule}
:::

::: {.card-item}
#### Behaviour, nutrition and health
Earlier and continuing work on the determinants of dietary intake — in
athletes, and in UK households through the cost-of-living crisis.

[Explore this research →](research.qmd#nutrition){.no-rule}
:::
:::
